name: 16d checkpoint interval
title: Picking a checkpoint interval
subtitle: 70B model on 2,048 GPUs; waste = checkpoint time / interval + interval / (2 x mean time between failures)

steps.caption: Llama 3 saw 419 unexpected interruptions in 54 days on 16,384 GPUs, one every 3.1 hours. At the same rate per GPU, 2,048 GPUs fail every 24.7 hours, and a failure loses half an interval of work on average.
A checkpoint stores master weights and both Adam moments, 12 bytes per parameter or 827.7 GB. At an assumed 10 GB/s of storage bandwidth, training waits 83 seconds per checkpoint.
Writing often wastes time on checkpoints, and writing rarely wastes work after failures. The total waste is the sum of the two curves.
The minimum sits where the two terms are equal, at the square root of 2 x 83 s x 24.7 h, which is 64 minutes or about 1,790 steps of 2.1 seconds. Each term is then 2.2% and the total 4.3%.
Copying the shards to host memory and writing them in the background cuts the blocking time to about a second. The best interval drops to 7 minutes and the waste to under 0.5%.
